questions.question: A state in a reversible chemical reaction where the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same speed is called which term?
questions.explanation: Chemical equilibrium is defined as the state in a reversible reaction where the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal.

questions.question: At chemical equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant because which condition is met?
options: Forward and reverse rates are equal
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal, so concentrations remain constant even though reactions continue.

questions.question: In the general reversible reaction A + B ⇌ C + D, the symbol ⇌ represents which property?
questions.explanation: The double arrow symbol ⇌ indicates that the reaction is reversible.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions illustrates a reversible reaction where the condition for forward and reverse reactions is the same?
questions.explanation: In the reaction 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(l) ⇌ Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g), the same condition applies for both forward and reverse reactions.

questions.question: In the reversible reaction NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g), the temperature conditions for the forward and reverse reactions are described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: For NH₄Cl, the forward and reverse reactions require different temperature conditions (heat for forward, cold for reverse).

questions.question: The equilibrium constant is a measure of the ratio of the concentration of the products to the concentration of the reactants, with each concentration raised to which power?
questions.explanation: Each concentration in the equilibrium constant expression is raised to the power corresponding to its coefficient in the balanced equation.

questions.question: For the reaction mA + nB ⇌ xC + yD, the equilibrium constant Kc is expressed as which formula?
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant Kc is the product of product concentrations raised to their coefficients divided by the product of reactant concentrations raised to their coefficients.

questions.question: In any equilibrium system containing a solid or pure liquid, the active mass of that substance is assumed to be which value?
questions.explanation: The active mass of a pure solid or pure liquid is assumed to be unity (1) at a given temperature.

questions.question: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the equilibrium constant Kc is expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Applying the equilibrium law, Kc = [NH₃]² / ([N₂][H₂]³) since the coefficients are 2, 1, and 3 respectively.

questions.question: For the reaction CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g), the equilibrium constant Kc simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Since CaCO₃ and CaO are solids, their active masses are 1, so Kc = [CO₂][1]/[1] = [CO₂].

questions.question: When a system in equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure or temperature, the equilibrium position shifts in order to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier's principle states that the system adjusts to oppose or cancel out the applied change.

questions.question: Le Chatelier's principle can also be stated as: if a system at equilibrium is disturbed, the system adjusts itself in order to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: The principle states that the system adjusts to restore equilibrium after a disturbance.

questions.question: The three major factors that affect the position of equilibrium are concentration, temperature, and which other factor?
questions.explanation: The three major factors affecting equilibrium position are changes in concentration, pressure, and temperature.

questions.question: An increase in the concentration of a reactant in an equilibrium system will shift the equilibrium position in which direction?
questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of a reactant shifts the equilibrium toward the formation of more products.

questions.question: A decrease in the concentration of a product in an equilibrium system will shift the equilibrium position in which direction?
questions.explanation: Removing product causes the system to shift toward the products to replace what was removed.

questions.question: Adding more H₂ to the equilibrium N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ will result in which change?
questions.explanation: Adding more H₂ (reactant) shifts the equilibrium to the right, producing more NH₃.

questions.question: For an exothermic forward reaction, an increase in temperature will shift the equilibrium position in which direction?
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature for an exothermic reaction shifts the equilibrium to the left (toward reactants) to absorb the added heat.

questions.question: For an endothermic forward reaction, an increase in temperature will shift the equilibrium position in which direction?
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature for an endothermic reaction shifts the equilibrium to the right (toward products).

questions.question: In the reaction 3H₂ + N₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (ΔH = -92 kJ), increasing the temperature affects the yield of ammonia in which way?
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is exothermic, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the left, decreasing ammonia yield.

questions.question: Increasing pressure by reducing volume in a gaseous equilibrium system will shift the equilibrium toward which side?
questions.explanation: Increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer moles of gas to reduce the pressure.

questions.question: For the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium in which direction?
questions.explanation: The left side has 4 moles of gas (1+3) and the right side has 2 moles, so increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (fewer moles).

questions.question: In the reaction PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), an increase in pressure will shift the equilibrium in which direction?
questions.explanation: The left side has 1 mole of gas and the right side has 2 moles, so increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the left (toward reactants).

questions.question: The presence of a catalyst in a reversible reaction has which effect on the equilibrium position?
questions.explanation: A catalyst increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions equally, so the equilibrium position is unchanged.

questions.question: A catalyst affects a reversible reaction by lowering the activation energies of the forward and backward reactions by which amount?
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of both forward and reverse reactions by the same amount, so equilibrium is reached faster but position is unchanged.

questions.question: When a noble gas is introduced into a system at equilibrium, which property of the system is increased?
questions.explanation: Adding a noble gas increases only the total pressure of the system without affecting partial pressures or concentrations.

questions.question: The addition of a noble gas to an equilibrium system has which effect on the equilibrium position?
questions.explanation: Since noble gases do not affect the partial pressures or concentrations of the reacting gases, the equilibrium position is unaffected.

questions.question: According to the one-sentence rules, increasing a reactant will cause the equilibrium to shift in which direction?
questions.explanation: Increasing a reactant shifts the equilibrium to the right to consume the added reactant.

questions.question: According to the one-sentence rules, increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with which characteristic?
questions.explanation: Increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles.

questions.question: According to the one-sentence rules, increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium away from which side?
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium away from the side that releases heat (i.e., favors the endothermic direction).

questions.question: According to the one-sentence rules, adding a catalyst causes which effect on equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Adding a catalyst results in no shift in equilibrium position, only a faster attainment of equilibrium.

questions.question: For the reaction PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), the equilibrium constant expression is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant K = [PCl₃][Cl₂] / [PCl₅].

questions.question: For the reaction PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), an increase in pressure will shift the equilibrium position in which direction?
questions.explanation: The left side has 1 mole of gas and the right side has 2 moles, so increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the left (backward reaction).

questions.question: For the reaction PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g) with ΔH = +95 kJ mol⁻¹, an increase in temperature will shift the equilibrium in which direction?
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is endothermic (ΔH positive), increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the right (forward reaction).

questions.question: For the reaction PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), the removal of chlorine will shift the equilibrium in which direction?
questions.explanation: Removing Cl₂ (a product) causes the system to shift right to produce more PCl₃ and Cl₂.

questions.question: In the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), if the concentration of NH₃ is increased, the equilibrium will shift in which direction?
questions.explanation: Increasing product concentration shifts the equilibrium to the left (toward reactants).

questions.question: The equilibrium constant Kc for a reaction is a measure of which property?
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant indicates the extent to which a reaction proceeds to form products.

questions.question: A reversible reaction is one in which the products can react to form which substances?
questions.explanation: In a reversible reaction, products can react to reform the original reactants.

questions.question: In the reaction I(s) ⇌ I(g), the temperature conditions for the forward and reverse reactions are described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: For iodine, the forward and reverse reactions require different temperature conditions (heat for sublimation, cold for deposition).

questions.question: The active mass of a pure solid in an equilibrium expression is taken as which value?
questions.explanation: Pure solids have a constant active mass of 1, so they are omitted from the equilibrium expression.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor that affects the position of equilibrium?
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up the attainment of equilibrium but does not change the equilibrium position.

questions.question: In Le Chatelier's principle, the system adjusts itself to do which of the following after a disturbance?
questions.explanation: The system adjusts to oppose the change and restore equilibrium.

questions.question: For an endothermic reaction, decreasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium in which direction?
questions.explanation: Decreasing temperature favors the exothermic direction, which is the reverse for an endothermic forward reaction.

questions.question: The equilibrium constant expression for the reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Applying the equilibrium law, Kc = [SO₃]² / ([SO₂]²[O₂]).

questions.question: In the reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium in which direction?
questions.explanation: The left side has 3 moles of gas and the right side has 2 moles, so increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (fewer moles).

questions.question: The equilibrium constant is temperature-dependent, meaning its value changes with which factor?
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant Kc depends on temperature and changes when temperature changes.

questions.question: In a reaction where ΔH is negative (exothermic), decreasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium in which direction?
questions.explanation: Decreasing temperature favors the exothermic direction, which is the forward reaction, shifting equilibrium right.

questions.question: A reversible reaction reaches equilibrium when which condition is achieved?
options: Forward and reverse rates become equal
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is reached when the rates of forward and reverse reactions become equal.

questions.question: Adding a catalyst to a reversible reaction increases the rate of which reaction(s)?
questions.explanation: A catalyst increases both forward and reverse reaction rates equally.

questions.question: In the reaction CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g), the active mass of CaO is given which value?
questions.explanation: Since CaO is a solid, its active mass is 1 and it is omitted from the equilibrium expression.

questions.question: The equilibrium constant expression for the reaction 4NH₃(g) + 5O₂(g) ⇌ 4NO(g) + 6H₂O(g) is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Applying the equilibrium law, Kc = [NO]⁴[H₂O]⁶ / ([NH₃]⁴[O₂]⁵).
